description: DoriaNET: A visual dataset from Hurricane Dorian for post-disaster building damage assessment is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Arash Noshadravan, Texas A&M University (tamu.edu). DoriaNET is a synthetic dataset for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based post-hurricane building damage assessment. DoriaNET consists of damage state annotations in accordance with FEMA Hurricane Model HAZUS-MH MR3 Manual. For each building, a damage state is manually assigned by closely matching the quantitative damage description of that building. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-gqvg-qx37. Keywords: Hurricane Dorian, Post-disaster damage assessment, UAV, Visual dataset, Building damage. Published 2021-10-18. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
